login.title: Log in
login.hint: User {user}. A fresh system has the password {password}.

password.title: Change password
password.forced: Before you start, change the default password. It is also the SSH password of the {user} user.

setup.title: Welcome to SuplaOS
setup.langIntro: Choose the language of the panel and the system.
setup.systemIntro: Time zone and the name of the device in your network.
setup.hostnameHelp: The panel will be at https://{name}.local:8443
setup.suplaIntro: Install your own Supla server now? It takes a few minutes, the images are downloaded from the internet. You can also do it later in Add-ons.
setup.accountHelp: Optional: an account in your Supla Cloud, created right after installing, without e-mail confirmation. It can also be done later on the Supla page.
setup.restoreIntro: Choose a full backup of the other device. The add-ons and their data come back as they were there, the settings you just chose stay.

addon.updateHelp: Downloads new images and recreates the containers (a backup is made first).
addon.cloudLoginHelp: Makes an OAuth app of SUPLA Scripts in the Supla Cloud of this device, with the account given here (the password is used only for this, not saved). Then SUPLA Scripts offers logging in with Supla Cloud and gets changes of the channels right away.
addon.cloudLoginDone: SUPLA Scripts has an OAuth app. Connecting again with another account makes an app of that account.
addon.backupsHelp: Restoring replaces the current data with the backup, a backup of the current data is made first. Keep downloaded backups off the device; upload one to move the data to a new device.
addon.restoreConfirm: Restore {name} from {file}? The current data will be replaced (a backup of it is made first) and the add-on is unavailable for a moment.
addon.accountHelp: Creates an account in your Supla Cloud, without e-mail confirmation.
addon.noDevices: No serial devices found. Plug in the coordinator and refresh.
addon.noLan: Not reachable from the local network, see the settings below.
addon.tlsHelp: The certificate is self-signed: add it as trusted (CA) in the MQTT client or turn off certificate verification.
addon.upToDate: The images are up to date (checked every few hours and with the update check).

system.title: System
system.networkWarn: After the change the panel may be at a new address: {address}
system.certificateIntro: The panel, the Supla Cloud and the add-ons use certificates of this device. Install its CA certificate once on each computer and phone you use, and the browser stops warning about them.
system.fingerprint: SHA-256 fingerprint, to compare with the one shown when installing:
system.poweroffConfirm: Shut down the device? You will need physical access to turn it on.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi
wifi.setupIntro: Connect the device to Wi-Fi now if you want to unplug the cable later. You can also do it later in System, Network.
wifi.noDevice: No Wi-Fi card found. If the device has one, it may need firmware the system doesn't have.
wifi.hotspotOn: no network, the device makes its own: {ssid}. Pick your Wi-Fi below.
wifi.passwordHelp: Leave it empty for an open network.
wifi.connectingAsync: Connecting to {ssid}. The panel is opened over Wi-Fi, so it may stop responding for a moment. If it doesn't come back, find the device by its name or on the list of devices in your router.
wifi.connectingHotspot: Connecting to {ssid}. The network {hotspot} goes off now: connect the phone back to {ssid} and open http://{host}.local (or find the device in the list of your router). If the password was wrong, {hotspot} comes back in about 3 minutes.
wifi.forgetConfirm: Forget the network {name}? The device disconnects from it if it is connected.
wifi.forgetAsync: The network is forgotten. The panel was opened over it, so it may stop responding.
wifi.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect from {ssid}? The device doesn't join any Wi-Fi network on its own until you connect again or restart it.
wifi.disconnectAsync: Disconnecting. The panel was opened over Wi-Fi, so it stops responding at this address.
wifi.autoconnectHelp: When the network is in range, also after a restart.

fullBackup.title: Full backup
fullBackup.intro: All add-ons with their settings and data, and the CA certificate of the device, in one file. Use it to move to another device or to keep a copy off the device.
fullBackup.passwordHelp: At least 8 characters. Without it the backup cannot be restored, keep it safe.
fullBackup.noPasswordWarn: The file holds the passwords of the add-ons, the accounts of the Supla Cloud and the key of the CA. Anyone who gets it can read them.
fullBackup.created: Backup saved, download it from the list.
fullBackup.restoreConfirm:
{info}

All add-ons and their data on this device are replaced. A full backup of the current state is made first. Restore?
fullBackup.restoreSetupConfirm:
{info}

The images of the add-ons are downloaded from the internet, it takes a few minutes. Restore?
fullBackup.setupIntro: A file suplaos-....tar.gz or .tar.gz.age, made on the Backups page of the other device.
fullBackup.restored: Restored. Supla devices connect to the server address they have: if it was the address of the old device, give this one the same address or change it in them.

backups.title: Backups
backups.addons: Backups of the database of one add-on alone (Supla, SUPLA Scripts) are on the page of that add-on.

autoBackup.title: Automatic backups
autoBackup.device: On the disk of the device
autoBackup.deviceHelp: Good against a mistake, not against a broken device or disk: better a share on another computer.
autoBackup.guestHelp: Without a user the share is opened as a guest.
autoBackup.nfsHelp: The NAS has to let this device write there (root squash off, or the export owned by the mapped user).
autoBackup.keepHelp: Older automatic backups are deleted. Backups made by hand stay.
autoBackup.passwordHelp: Kept on the device, so that the backups can be encrypted at night. You need it to restore them: write it down.
autoBackup.testOK: The share works, a test file was written and deleted.

sshKeys.title: SSH keys
sshKeys.intro: Public keys that log in over SSH as {user} without the password.
sshKeys.help: One line from a .pub file, e.g. ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub on your computer (ssh-keygen -t ed25519 makes one).
sshKeys.deleteConfirm: Delete the key {name}? It will no longer log in.

fan.title: Fan
fan.pi5: The fan connector of the Pi 5 (Active Cooler) is controlled by the firmware, it needs nothing here.
fan.argonHelp: It starts at 30% and speeds up to 100%. It stops a few degrees below the start, so that it does not start and stop all the time.
fan.buttonHelp: Pressing it twice quickly restarts the system, holding it for about 3 s shuts it down properly, then the case cuts the power.
fan.gpioHelp: The official Raspberry Pi 4 case fan is on GPIO 14, the Pimoroni Fan SHIM on GPIO 18. The fan goes off 10 °C below. The kernel switches it, also when the panel does not run.
fan.rebootNeeded: Restart the device to apply the fan settings.

migration.title: Move from another Supla Cloud
migration.intro: Moves your account on the public Supla Cloud (or another own server) here: devices, channels, locations, access IDs, channel groups, scenes, schedules, reactions, direct links, icons and the measurement history. Devices and channels keep their IDs, so the apps, MQTT, Home Assistant and scripts that use them keep working.
migration.token: Personal access token of the source account
migration.tokenHelp: In that Supla Cloud: Account, Security, Personal access tokens. Turn on Read in every section except Client’s Apps (Modification is not needed), and for SUPLA Scripts also Channels: execute actions. It is kept until the move ends, for the measurement history, and deleted then.
migration.prepareHelp: The devices register with the e-mail of the account, so the account here is {email}. It is made with this password when there is none. The Supla here has to be fresh: without devices or locations of the same IDs.
migration.prepareConfirm: The devices, channels, locations and access IDs are added to the Supla here with their IDs. Then switch the devices one by one to this server. Continue?
migration.switch: Switch every device to the server {server}: in its configuration page (GUI-Generic, SuplaDevice), in the Supla Config app for factory devices, or in the options of Zigbee2Supla. When it connects, it gets its settings within a minute.
migration.errors: {n} devices connected, but some settings were not accepted, see the list.
migration.cancelConfirm: Forget the account read from the source?
migration.cancelPreparedConfirm: End the move? Devices that connect later do not get their settings any more. What was added to the Supla here stays.
migration.notMade: Not moved, set them again here:
migration.links: Direct links get new addresses here, change them where you use them:
migration.history: Measurement history: {n} log items, last copied {date}.
migration.historyHelp: The source keeps logging until a device is switched here. Copy the newer history after switching the devices, before you end the move.
migration.scriptsHelp: Scenes, thermostats and notifications of SUPLA Scripts of the source account move to SUPLA Scripts here. They refer to the channels by the IDs the move keeps. An account that logs in there only through Supla Cloud needs a username and password first (SUPLA Scripts login page: other ways to log in, link with a private Supla Cloud by a token). Phones for notifications are registered again in the app.
migration.scriptsURL: Address of the source SUPLA Scripts
migration.scriptsTokenHelp: Only if the token of the move has no Channels: execute actions. It is used for this and not kept.

suplaDevices.title: CA certificate for devices (Custom CA)
suplaDevices.intro: In the settings of a device (GUI-Generic, SuplaDevice: Supla protocol) set the server {server}, the e-mail of your account and the security level Custom CA, and paste this certificate (PEM) there, with the BEGIN and END lines. The device then checks it connects to this server.
suplaDevices.help: Devices without the Custom CA option (older firmware) connect with Skip certificate verification. The certificate stays the same when the address of the device changes and after moving to another device with a full backup.

jobTitle.connectScripts: Connecting SUPLA Scripts with Supla Cloud
jobTitle.prepareMove: Preparing the move from Supla Cloud

power.rebootText: The device is restarting. The panel opens again on its own when it's back, usually after a minute or two.
power.slow: It takes longer than usual. Check the device, this page keeps waiting.
power.offText: Wait a few seconds before unplugging it (on a Raspberry Pi until the green LED stops blinking).
power.waiting: When you turn it on again, this page opens the panel on its own.

updates.title: Updates
updates.confirm: Update the system now? The panel restarts on the way, add-ons keep running.
updates.running: Updating, the panel may disappear for a moment...
updates.rebootRequired: A new kernel is installed, restart the device to use it.
updates.addonsText: SuplaOS brought new versions of: {list}. Applying them recreates their containers (a backup is made first), so they are unavailable for a moment.
updates.auto: Install Debian security and stable updates every day
updates.autoHelp: SuplaOS itself and the Raspberry Pi kernel are updated only from this page. The device is not restarted automatically.
updates.imagesText: There are newer container images of these add-ons. Update them on the add-on page with the Update button.

domain.title: Own domain (Let's Encrypt)
domain.intro: With your own domain (or a free name at DuckDNS or deSEC) the device gets a Let's Encrypt certificate, which browsers and apps trust without installing the CA. The DNS provider has to have an API: SuplaOS sets a TXT record there, the device doesn't have to be reachable from the internet.
domain.domainHelp: e.g. supla.example.com. Supla Cloud, the panel and the add-ons answer at this name, so it should point to the address of the device.
domain.providerHelp: Where the DNS of the domain is kept. A domain at a registrar without an API can use DuckDNS or deSEC through a CNAME record.
domain.emailHelp: Of the Let's Encrypt account. Not needed.
domain.staging: Test server of Let's Encrypt (the certificate won't be trusted)
domain.disableConfirm: Turn off the domain? The add-ons go back to the certificate of the device and the keys of the DNS provider are removed.
domain.addresses: These addresses could be the domain now, then they also work without warnings:
domain.addressesOAuth: SUPLA Scripts logs in with Supla Cloud: after the change connect them again.
domain.reconnect: Done. Now connect SUPLA Scripts with Supla Cloud again: Add-ons, SUPLA Scripts, Connect with Supla Cloud.
